description_en: IlāyBahīis one of the majorbahīsin Patan. Thebāhī, including the shrine of the primary deity,dyaḥchẽ, was abandoned after the demise of the members of itssaṅgha. Local residents started to pay attention to it only after a Buddhist nun cleaned up the ruins and started to live here.On the request of the locals, the Department of Archaeology rebuilt thedyaḥchẽin VS 2044 (1987 CE). It has two stories and tiled with thejhĩgaṭībricks. Unlike thedyaḥchẽsof otherbahīs, thisdyaḥchẽhas nophujāabove its roof. The plain struts are supporting both of its roofs. Thedyaḥchẽ’sfirst floor has atrikhājhyāḥflanked by two small simple windows. Agandhakuṭī,having the shape of a three-bayedphalcā,is established in its first floor and surrounded by open space in order to facilitate the devotees to circumambulate it. The main entrance to thegandhakuṭīhas notoraṇa. The stone statue of Akṣobhya, enshrined as thegandhurī devatāin the sanctum inside thegandhakuṭī,got stolen long ago, thus Satya Vajrācārya, a resident of Bhindya Bāhāḥ (LAL1880) installed a new Akṣobhya statue in around 2015-2016 CE (VS 2072-2073) at the same place where the stolen statue was enshrined.ADharmadhātu Maṇdalaand fourcaityasare installed on thebahī’s courtyard. Although there are no evidence to appoint the initial construction of thebahī, the presence of twoLicchavi Caityasin the courtyard suggests that it was built during the Licchavi Period. After the demise of thebahī’ssaṅghamembers,the daughter of one of the deceasedsaṅghamembers sponsored the daily rituals of thebahī. In the present-day (September 2020), the Vajrācārya women from Bhindya Bāhāḥ have been performing these rituals.Its anniversary ritual,varṣavardhanapūjā, which used to take place annually on the seventh lunar day of the dark fortnight of Kārtika, has been discontinued for many years. The Lalitpur Metropolitan Office financed the renovation of the northeast face of thebāhīcourtyard in VS 2071 (2014 CE), and its southeast face is under renovation as of September 202). A Buddhist monk and nun are living in thebahīin the present-day.
description_ne: यो ललितपुरका प्रमुख बहीहरूमध्ये एक हो । यो बहीका संघ सदस्यहरूको मृत्यु भएपछि धेरै वर्षसम्म बेवारिसे अवस्थामा रहेको थियो । बहीको द्य:छेँ भत्केर भग्नावशेष बनिसकेको थियो । भग्नावशेष सफा गरी एकजना भिक्षुणी यहाँ बस्न आएपछि  बहीतर्फ मानिसहरूको ध्यान गयो । स्थानीयहरूको प्रयासमा पुरातत्व विभागमा अनुरोध गरी विसं २०४४ सालतिर बहीको द्य:छेँको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।दुई तलाको द्य:छेँमा झिंगटीको छाना राखिएको छ । यो बही भएपनि छानामाथि पुर (फुचा) राखिएको छैन । छानाको भार थाम्न सादा टुँडालहरू राखिएका छन् । द्य:छेँको पहिलो तलाको बीचमा त्रिखाझ्या राखी दायाँबायाँ एक-एकवटा साना झ्यालहरू राखिएका छन् । द्य:छेँको भुइँतला तीनवटा कवल भएको फल्चाको स्वरुप बनाई गन्धकुटी स्थापना गरिएको छ । गन्धकुटीको परिक्रमा गर्न प्रदक्षिणापथ बनाइएको छ । गन्धकुटीभित्र पस्ने ढोकामाथि कुनै तोरण राखिएको छैन । गन्धकुटीभित्र ढुंगाको अक्षोभ्यलाई गन्धुरी देवताको रूपमा स्थापना गरिएको छ । पुरानो मूर्ति चोरी भएपछि वर्षौंसम्म गन्धुरी देवताबिना नै बहीको पूजाआजा चलिरहेको थियो । विसं २०७२-७३ सालतिर भिन्द्य: बाहा: (LAL1880) का सत्य वज्राचार्यले नयाँ मूर्ति बनाएर स्थापना गरेका थिए ।बही प्राङ्गनमा एउटा धर्मधातु मण्डलका साथमा चारवटा चैत्य स्थापना गरिएका छन् । यो बही कहिले बनाइएको थियो भन्ने कुरा स्पष्ट पार्ने कुनै ऐतिहासिक सामग्री पाइँदैन । तर बही प्राङ्गनमा दुईवटा लिच्छवि चैत्यहरू गाडिएर रहेकोले लिच्छविकालमा नै बनिसकेको अनुमान गर्न सकिन्छ । बहीका सबै संघ सदस्यहरूको मृत्यु भइसकेकोले एकजना संघ सदस्यकी छोरीको तर्फबाट बहीको नित्यपूजा सञ्चालन भइरहेको छ । अहिले भिन्द्य: बाहा:मा बस्ने वज्राचार्य महिलाले नित्यपूजा गरिरहेका छन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष कार्तिक कृष्ण ७ मा गरिने बहीको वर्षबन्धन पूजा भने बन्द भइसकेको छ । ललितपुर महानगरपालिकाको आर्थिक सहयोगमा विसं २०७१ (सन् २०१४) मा बहीको उत्तर-पूर्वी भागको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो भने दक्षिण-पूर्वी भागको पुनर्निर्माणको काम भइरहेको छ । अहिले यस बहीमा एक भिक्षु र एक भिक्षुणी बसिरहेका छन् ।

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a New Akṣobhya Statue
historical_events.event_description: The stone statue of Akṣobhya, enshrined in the sanctum inside thegandhakuṭī,was stolen long ago. Around VS 2072-2073 (2015-2016 CE), Satya Vajrācārya, a resident of Bhindya Bāhāḥ (LAL1880), installed a new Akṣobhya statue at the same place where the stolen statue was enshrined.

historical_events.event_name: Renovation of the Bahī's Northeast Part
historical_events.event_description: The Lalitpur Metropolitan Office gave thirty-two lakhs rupees for the renovation of the northeast part of thebāhīin VS 2071 (2014 CE).

historical_events.event_name: Renovation of the Bahī's Southeast Part
historical_events.event_description: The bahī's southeast part is under renovation as of September 2020 with the financial support of twenty-four lakhs rupeesthe of Lalitpur Metropolitan City Office. Since the allocated budget was not sufficient to complete the renovation process, the Metropolitan City office has recently decided to allocate an additional twenty-five lakhs rupees.
Two statues of a male and a female donor were established on thebahī’s courtyard.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of Statues of Vajrasattva, Vasundharā, and Nāmasaṅgīti
historical_events.event_description: The local residents installed the statues of Vajrasattva, Vasundharā, and Nāmasaṅgīti on the ground floor of one of thebahī’s buildings which is under construction.

Purṇarāja (text: Punarāja) and his younger brother Nhukṣerāja constructed the Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala at thebahī's courtyard in the memory of their deceased father Harṣajyoti (text: Harṣajoti) and mother Ratna Thakũ.
On the request of the locals, the Department of Archaeology rebuilt thedyaḥchẽin VS 2044 (1987 CE).
